title: Exact derived localization preserves pasting of noninvertible transformations
statement: Let a finite diagram of abelian categories with chosen ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be given. Label its edges by additive exact functors and its cells by natural transformations between composites of edges; these transformations need not be invertible. Write $C(F)$ for degreewise application and choose $D(F)$ with the standard factorization $D(F)Q\simeq QC(F)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For $t:F_2F_1\to H_2H_1$, define $t^D:D(F_2)D(F_1)\to D(H_2)D(H_1)$ as inverse exact-composition comparison, localization of $C(t)$, and forward exact-composition comparison. Derive each specified compositor isomorphism in the same way. Then every equality between finite composites and whiskerings of these cells and compositors passes to the corresponding equality on unbounded derived categories. In particular both vertical and horizontal square-pasting equations, naturality equations, and compositor unit equations pass with these precise comparisons. Invertible ordinary cells induce invertible derived cells; no resolution, boundedness assumption or faithfulness of an evaluation functor is needed.

proof.text: Use right-to-left composition throughout. For a word $P=F_r\cdots F_1$ of composable edges let $C(P)$ be its termwise functor and $T_P=D(F_r)\cdots D(F_1)$. An empty word denotes the identity. If $t:P\to R$ is an ordinary cell, its components $t_{K^i}$ form a complex morphism $C(t)_K$, since naturality at $d_K^i$ says $R(d_K^i)t_{K^i}=t_{K^{i+1}}P(d_K^i)$. Naturality at complex morphisms is likewise degreewise. Termwise application preserves identities, vertical composition, and either whiskering: each assertion is the same equality at each $K^i$. Thus every given ordinary equation is an equation of transformations of complex functors.

proof.text:
Every composite of the edges is additive and exact: apply the two functors successively to a finite limiting or colimiting cone. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], each $C(F)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and has its chosen natural factorization $a_F:D(F)Q\xrightarrow{\sim}QC(F)$. For a word define a natural isomorphism $a_P:T_PQ\xrightarrow{\sim}QC(P)$ recursively by $a_{\varnothing}=1_Q$ and
$$a_{FP,K}=a_{F,C(P)K}\circ D(F)(a_{P,K}).$$
Consequently $T_P$ is a lift of the quasi-isomorphism-inverting functor $QC(P)$. The compositor of [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] is in the direction $\mu_{F,G}:D(GF)\to D(G)D(F)$ and satisfies $a_{GF\text{ as a word},K}\mu_{F,G,QK}=a_{GF,K}$, where the last factor is the chosen factorization for the single exact functor $GF$. This fixes the direction of every comparison used below.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q$ is a localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with target $D(\mathcal B)$, the functors $Q_{\mathcal B}C(P),Q_{\mathcal B}C(R)$, lifts $T_P,T_R$ and lifting isomorphisms $a_P,a_R$. It gives the unique transformation $t^D:T_P\to T_R$ characterized by
$$(*)\qquad a_{R,K}\circ t^D_{QK}=Q(C(t)_K)\circ a_{P,K}.$$
For two-edge words, first lift $C(t)$ between the single functors $D(F_2F_1),D(H_2H_1)$. The equation for $\mu$ in [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] shows that conjugating this lift by $\mu_H$ and $\mu_F^{-1}$ satisfies $(*)$. Uniqueness identifies it with $t^D$. This is precisely inverse source composition comparison, localized cell, forward target composition comparison as required, including for a specified ordinary compositor.

proof.text:
For $t:P\to R$ and $s:R\to S$, equation $(*)$ gives
$$a_S\,s^D_{QK}t^D_{QK}=Q(C(s)_K)\,a_Rt^D_{QK}=Q(C(s\circ t)_K)\,a_P.$$
For the identity cell the same formula is $a_P1=Q(1)a_P$. Cancellation of $a_S$ (respectively $a_P$) and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identify the lifts with $s^D\circ t^D$ and $1_{T_P}$, respectively. This proves the vertical-composition and identity rules without cancelling a cell.

proof.text:
For output whiskering, let $V$ be an additional word with source the target of $P,R$. Use $a_{VP,K}=a_{V,C(P)K}\,T_V(a_{P,K})$ and the analogous formula for $VR$; this follows by expanding the recursion in Step 2. Naturality of $a_V$ at the complex morphism $C(t)_K$ gives the full calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
a_{VR,K}\,T_V(t^D_{QK})
&=a_{V,C(R)K}\,T_V(a_{R,K}t^D_{QK})\\
&=a_{V,C(R)K}\,T_V(Q(C(t)_K))\,T_V(a_{P,K})\\
&=Q(C(V)(C(t)_K))\,a_{V,C(P)K}\,T_V(a_{P,K})\\
&=Q(C(Vt)_K)\,a_{VP,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identifies this whiskered transformation with $(Vt)^D$. For single-composite derived functors insert the comparisons normalized in Step 2; conjugation by them gives the same formula.

proof.text:
For input whiskering let $U$ be a word ending at the source of $P,R$. Naturality of the already constructed transformation $t^D:T_P\to T_R$ at the derived morphism $a_{U,K}:T_UQK\to QC(U)K$ says
$$T_R(a_{U,K})\,t^D_{T_UQK}=t^D_{QC(U)K}\,T_P(a_{U,K}).$$
Multiplying by $a_{R,C(U)K}$ and applying $(*)$ to the complex $C(U)K$ yields
$$a_{RU,K}\,t^D_{T_UQK}=Q(C(t)_{C(U)K})\,a_{P,C(U)K}\,T_P(a_{U,K})=Q(C(tU)_K)\,a_{PU,K}.$$
Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now gives $(tU)^D=t^DT_U$, with the prescribed comparisons if a composite is represented by one derived functor. This uses naturality on the actual derived morphism $a_{U,K}$; it does not assume that this morphism comes from a complex morphism.

proof.text:
For completeness the canonical comparison $c_P:D(P)\to T_P$ is the lift of the identity of $QC(P)$, using the chosen single-functor factorization $a_{P\mathrm{,single}}$ and the word factorization $a_P$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes it an isomorphism with $a_Pc_{P,QK}=a_{P\mathrm{,single}}$. For a two-edge word it is exactly $\mu$ by [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition]. For three consecutive edges $F,G,H$, the word factorization is explicitly
$$a_{H,C(G)C(F)K}\,D(H)(a_{G,C(F)K})\,D(H)D(G)(a_{F,K}).$$
Write $b=a_{HGF\text{ as a word},K}$. For $l=D(H)(\mu_{F,G})\mu_{GF,H}$ the two-edge equations give $bl_{QK}=a_{H,C(GF)K}D(H)(a_{GF,K})\mu_{GF,H,QK}=a_{HGF,K}$. For $r=(\mu_{G,H}D(F))\mu_{F,HG}$, naturality of $\mu_{G,H}$ at $a_{F,K}$ first gives $br_{QK}=a_{HG,C(F)K}D(HG)(a_{F,K})\mu_{F,HG,QK}=a_{HGF,K}$. Here $a_{HGF,K}$ is the factorization for the single composite functor. Cancel $b$ and apply clause (3) to obtain $l=r$. The same argument is induction on the length of a word: length one is $c_F=1$; appending the next edge uses the recursion for $a_P$ and the two-edge equation, so each iterated comparison is the unique normalized $c_P$. For length zero, lifting $1_Q$ between $D(1)$ and $1_{D(\mathcal A)}$ gives the canonical unit comparison with component $a_{1,K}$ at $QK$. Inserting it in either side of a word gives the same normalization, hence both compositor unit equations. No extra coherence theorem is assumed.

proof.text: Induct on a finite expression made from the specified cells and compositors by identities, vertical composition and either whiskering. Its base case is $(*)$ from Step 3, including ordinary compositor cells; identity and composition cases are Step 4; the two whiskering cases are Steps 5 and 6. Step 7 identifies all inserted comparisons with precisely the chosen exact-composition and unit comparisons. Thus an expression $E:P\to R$ always satisfies $a_R E^D_{QK}=Q(C(E)_K)a_P$. If $E=E'$ is one of the given ordinary equations, Step 1 gives $C(E)=C(E')$ and hence equality of these normalized components. Cancel $a_R$ and apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. This proves $E^D=E'^D$. In particular a horizontal paste is output whiskering followed by input whiskering and vertical composition, so both square-pasting orientations and all specified naturality and compositor unit equations follow.

proof.text: If $t$ is invertible, apply the construction also to $t^{-1}$. Step 4 applied to the two ordinary inverse equations shows $(t^{-1})^Dt^D=1$ and $t^D(t^{-1})^D=1$. Thus $t^D$ is invertible. The only descent hypotheses used were that the word functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, supplied by exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and that $Q$ is a localization. All complexes were unrestricted $\mathbf Z$-indexed complexes throughout; no resolutions or evaluation functors occurred.

Its direction is mu: D(GF) -> D(G)D(F) with a_{G,C(F)K} D(G)(a_{F,K}) mu_{QK} = a_{GF,K}, matching every use. Sources: Stacks Tag 015F (derived.tex 5883-5903) and Tag 04VG (categories.tex 4406), both checked in the tags file. Mathlib Localization liftNatTrans and natTrans_ext are at Predicate.lean 278-361. Clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property lifts transformations that need not be invertible. I recomputed every step myself. Step 3 gives the normalization (*), and conjugating by mu_H and mu_F^{-1} gives the same lift by uniqueness. Step 4 covers vertical composition and identities. In Step 5, output whiskering uses the a_{VP} expansion by induction and naturality of a_V at C(t)_K. In Step 6, input whiskering uses naturality of t^D at the derived morphism a_{U,K}. In Step 7, the three-edge coherence holds: b*l and b*r both equal a_{HGF,K}, with naturality of mu_{G,H} at a_{F,K}. The word-length induction and the unit comparison D(1)->1 are set up with base and step. Step 8 is a properly stated induction on expressions, and Step 9 gives invertibility. No cell is ever cancelled. Zero cells, empty words and unbounded complexes behave correctly.
